lesson.menu_title: The Live Wire — Second Simulation, Unknown Evaluator
lesson.menu_desc: What a second evaluator scores, and why the same answer twice is the evidence -- 26 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 12 -- The Live Wire
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernando Meneghelli Bottura | Lesson 12 -- The Live Wire

listenings.text: People imagine the scorecard is about language, and it never is. Ours has four lines. Structure: does the answer have a shape, or does it wander until the candidate runs out of air. Evidence: is there a number, a date or a name in it. Recovery: what happens after a question that does not go well, because something always does not go well. And consistency: is this the same story we heard in the first round, with the same figures. That last line is where most people lose points, and almost nobody prepares for it. They prepare new material instead, which is exactly the wrong instinct. If your first answer was good, give the same one. We are not bored. We are checking.

At the end I ask every candidate the same thing: what would make you say no to us. Most of them tell me there is nothing, and that answer costs them. It tells me either that they have not thought about it, or that they will say anything to get the offer, and I do not want either of those people running my finance function. The answers I remember are specific. One man told me he would say no if the reporting line to the board went through somebody else, because he had lived that once. I disagreed with him about the structure, and I hired him anyway, because I knew exactly what I was getting. Say the true thing. It is the only answer in that conversation that cannot be checked, and it is the one I trust.

extra_audio.text: Claire says the second evaluator is somebody he has not met. Fernando asks what the round will be scored on. Claire names structure, evidence and consistency with round one. Fernando decides to give exactly the same figures as before. Claire warns him about the question on what would make him say no.
